title: Using Generative Adversarial Networks for Event Log Generation (Master Thesis - Wei-Yi Chen)
summary: A master's thesis project that generates synthetic business-process event logs using GAN-based tabular models, including a custom differentially-private CTGAN variant (DPCTGAN) built on top of a vendored, modified copy of the SDV codebase. The thesis's main.py and checkpoint.py directly instantiate sdv.tabular.ctgan.CTGAN and subclass ctgan's CTGANSynthesizer, running SDV's CTGAN wrapper and constraints as the core generative-modeling pipeline for the experiments.
evidence: main.py:5-8 imports CTGANSynthesizer, sdv.tabular.ctgan.CTGAN, DPCTGAN, sdv.constraints.Positive; DPCTGAN.py:308 class DPCTGAN(CTGANSynthesizer)
needs: Repository contains a full vendored copy of the SDV package (sdv/, docs/developer_guides/sdv) modified with a custom DPCTGAN; unclear if this constitutes a genuine fork submission versus thesis code, flagged as possibly first-party-adjacent work.

title: What's Wrong with Your Synthetic Tabular Data? Using Explainable AI to Evaluate Generative Models

title: DP-CGANS (Differentially Private - Conditional Generative Adversarial NetworkS)
summary: A differentially-private conditional GAN library that generates synthetic tabular (and RDF-derived) personal health data, wrapping and modifying a conditional matrix/cost function inside a copied CTGAN implementation. It is built directly by extending and modifying SDV's CTGAN synthesizer source code (ctgan/synthesizers/ctgan.py, data_sampler.py, data_transformer.py) alongside rdt- and copulas-derived transformer and distribution code.
affiliations: Institute of Data Science, Maastricht University
